subject: DPA: onshore processing & deletion SLA options for EU production data
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarification: EU onshore processing + deletion SLA

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two procurement items popped up after reviewing the DPA draft:

1) Residency requirement — Acme must ensure that patient-derived inputs and derived artifacts for production workloads are processed and stored within EU boundaries unless an explicit onshore exception is approved. Can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee processing in an EU region for hosted API customers, and what options exist for onshore-only processing?

2) Deletion SLA — we need a firm contractual window for data erasure after an erasure request. Our legal team expects a 30-calendar-day completion for all production data (including backups). Is that achievable, and what language would Redwood need in the DPA to commit to this?

Also please attach any retention/backup carve-outs (e.g., disaster recovery windows) so our security team can evaluate.

Thanks — looking to get this cleared before our procurement committee on Dec 8.

Karen Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Attachment: None

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification: EU onshore processing + deletion SLA

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, then proposed redline language below.

Residency: For hosted customers we can pin workloads to an EU region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam) and guarantee that ingress, inference, and primary persistent storage remain in-region. For stronger guarantees (onshore-only processing with customer-managed keys and network controls) we can offer Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated pools with on-prem routing.

Deletion SLA: Our standard hosted offering commits to logical deletion of primary production data within 30 days of a verified erasure request. Backups are purged on a staggered schedule; typical backup retention windows are up to 60 days for rapid recovery, and irrecoverable deletion from snapshots within 90 days.

Proposed redline language (draft):
"For Customers electing EU-region processing, Redwood will ensure that Customer Data in primary production stores and inference processing occurs within EU geographic boundaries. Customer Data will be logically deleted from primary production stores within thirty (30) calendar days of a verified erasure request. Redwood maintains backups and immutable snapshots only for disaster recovery; such backups shall be retained no longer than sixty (60) calendar days and shall be irrecoverably deleted no later than ninety (90) calendar days from the time of the initial deletion request, except where retention is required by applicable law. Redwood shall provide Customer with confirmation of deletion upon completion."

Notes / options to discuss:
- If Acme requires strict 30-day end-to-end deletion (including backups), we need an exception for disaster recovery risk and may require Dedicated/Private deployment to meet the contractual commitment.
- We can offer an SLA-backed path for Dedicated customers with additional capacity and runbooks to shorten backup purge windows.
- We recommend adding an audit artifact: a deletion confirmation report and a log extract showing deletion events (hashes/ids), which we can provide as part of the compliance package.

I've attached a short summary (retention-deletion-options-summary.pdf) and a redlined DPA (DPA_Redlines_Acme_v3.docx) with both the standard wording and an accelerated timeline variant for Dedicated/Private. Please review and let me know which path your legal/security prefer.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-deletion-options-summary.pdf, DPA_Redlines_Acme_v3.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:22:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Clarification: EU onshore processing + deletion SLA — suggested legal language

Diego — forwarding Karen's note. Legal review notes below (high level).

Suggested tweak to proposed redline: replace the staggered "backups up to 60/90 days" wording with specific "backup retention tiers" so we don't commit to an absolute final purge window that might be impacted by cross-region DR restores. Example: 
"Backups retained for disaster recovery purposes shall be retained for no longer than ninety (90) calendar days under normal operating conditions. In the event of an active DR restore, Redwood will notify Customer and will complete purge activities as soon as reasonably practicable afterward."

Also add: "Where Customer elects Dedicated or Private deployment and requests contractual deletion within thirty (30) calendar days including backups, Redwood will provide a dedicated runbook and additional operational controls; such terms may be subject to an addendum and reasonable implementation fee."

Practical ask: do you have an example SOC2 deletion confirmation artifact we can share? If not, we should create a template ASAP.

—Marissa
Director, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: None

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 13:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification: EU onshore processing + deletion SLA — suggested legal language

Marissa — thanks, that framing is helpful. A couple practical items:

1) Karen's timeline is firm (procurement committee Dec 8). We need to finalize language and indicate which option (hosted EU + 60/90 backup window) vs Dedicated/Private with 30-day end-to-end deletion Acme should accept.

2) I have a basic deletion confirmation template (CSV with resource ids, timestamps, and hashed checksums) which I've used before; attaching it to the DPA redline packet and will convert to a SOC2-friendly artifact if Legal needs a different format.

3) Rishi — can you weigh in on whether we should offer a firm 30-day backup purge for Dedicated customers (and if an implementation fee is reasonable)? If yes, we should include a short schedule and the runbook reference in the redline.

Diego

Attachment: deletion-confirmation-template.csv

From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification: EU onshore processing + deletion SLA

Hi Diego — thanks for the detailed options and for looping Legal. We reviewed the draft and have two follow-ups before we present to the committee: 

1) The standard hosted wording is acceptable for initial procurement evaluation, provided we get an explicit note in the DPA that backups are treated as described and that any DR restore will be communicated within 24 hours. Could you add a single sentence committing to DR notification timing?

2) Acme prefers the Dedicated path if Redwood will contractually commit to an end-to-end 30-day deletion (including backups and snapshots). If you can confirm there will be an addendum with the runbook and an estimated one-time implementation fee, we can move forward with procurement contingent on that addendum and a DocuSign-ready DPA.

If you can get the redline with the DR notification sentence and a Dedicated addendum outline by EOD Dec 3, we should be able to make the Dec 8 procurement committee.

Thanks —
Karen

Attachment: None
